meta.title: Optimize Erlang runtime helpers
meta.body_summary: Minimize Erlang runtime output by tracking used helper functions in the compiler so only necessary helpers are included, reducing code size.

perf_labels.notes: OpenAI_Codex compiler optimization to emit only used Erlang helpers; self-merged without review or perf evidence; 246-line single-file change.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 246 changed lines in one file, this is a small-to-medium edit by absolute volume. As a self-contained compiler performance tweak, it fits the low-risk profile that justifies a fast merge without human review.

review_details.concern_detail: No review or comment text is available; the PR was self-merged by the author within minutes of creation.
review_details.performance_claim: Reduce Erlang runtime output size by conditionally including helper functions only when they are referenced.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: A compiler backend change to track helper usage; the agent produced a working optimization that passed tests and was merged immediately. However, absence of any benchmark suggests agents may not autonomously provide performance evidence.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark, profiling, or before/after metrics; only a narrative summary and `go test ./...` instruction.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No regression feedback or related issues observed; PR merged without further validation beyond the author's own testing.

core_change_summary.description: In compile/erlang/compiler.go, the Erlang code generator now tracks which runtime helper functions are actually referenced during code generation and emits only those, instead of always including all helpers.
change_trajectory: Single commit (be82dff): Added usage tracking for Erlang runtime helpers and conditional inclusion logic, with corresponding removal of unconditional helper emission.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened by tamnd with 'codex' label, immediately self-merged within ~4 minutes; no human review or comments.
